metadata.title: fix(llm): align Bedrock GatewayProvider config keys with DB schema
metadata.author: kimsehwan96

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Close: #3761

---

## 📝 Summary
`GatewayProvider.get_llm()` reads Bedrock credentials using boto3-style key names (`aws_access_key_id`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `region_name`), but the Admin UI stores them via `llm_provider_configs.AWSBedrockConfig` which uses shorter key names (`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `region`).

This mismatch causes `config.get("aws_access_key_id")` to always return `None`, silently falling back to the node IAM role instead of using the user-configured credentials.

commits.message:
fix(llm): align Bedrock GatewayProvider config keys with DB schema

The GatewayProvider bedrock branch reads aws_access_key_id,
aws_secret_access_key, and region_name from the provider config,
but llm_provider_configs.AWSBedrockConfig stores them as
access_key_id, secret_access_key, and region. This mismatch
causes credentials to silently fall back to the node IAM role.

Signed-off-by: kimsehwan96 <sktpghks138@gmail.com>
commits.author: kimsehwan96

commits.message:
test(llm): align Bedrock GatewayProvider tests with DB schema keys

Update existing tests to use DB schema key names (region,
access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token) instead of boto3-style
names. Add assertions verifying credentials are correctly mapped to
boto3 kwargs, and add tests for no-credentials and default-region
edge cases.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(llm): forward Bedrock profile_name to credentials_profile_name

The DB schema exposes profile_name via the Admin UI but
GatewayProvider never mapped it to the langchain-aws
credentials_profile_name kwarg, causing the same silent
IAM-fallback bug this PR fixes for access key credentials.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
